crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers optical, radar, multispectral, and thermal images from Earth observation satellites, used to measure economic activity that is not visible in standard financial statements or government releases.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data refers to anonymized records of purchases made with credit, debit, and prepaid cards, aggregated by merchant, category, geography, and time.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data as alternative data covers physical-world signals from vessel transponders, port sensors, weather stations and cargo telemetry, used to estimate trade flows, commodity supply, congestion and industrial activity.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data refers to aggregated or individual-level geospatial records collected from smartphones and other connected devices, used as an alternative dataset for economic analysis, retail footfall, mobility, and real estate.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection in alternative data means gathering publicly available information from websites, forums, job boards, app stores, social media, and regulatory filings to build datasets that supplement traditional financial and economic data.

sections.body: Alternative data means information gathered outside standard financial statements and market prices. It includes satellite photos of parking lots and crops, anonymized card spending records, readings from shipping and industrial sensors, location pings from mobile devices, and text or images pulled from public websites. Artificial intelligence is used now to turn these messy streams into usable signals. For example, computer vision models count cars in retail parking lots from satellite images to estimate foot traffic before earnings. Natural language processing reads job postings and product reviews from web collection to gauge company activity. The work is operational, not theoretical, with hedge funds and corporate strategy teams buying these feeds daily.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has solved some narrow problems well. Counting cars, ships, or oil tanks in clear imagery is reliable enough for routine use. Card transaction panels can track spending shifts by category and region within days. What remains unsolved is the jump from a clean count to a correct economic or investment conclusion. Noise, bias, and coverage gaps are large, and many vendors overstate how predictive their data is. Honest limits include poor performance in cloudy regions for satellite work, sparse sensor coverage outside major trade routes, and location data that skews toward certain phone users.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages under this section break the field into its main raw sources. Satellite Imagery covers what can be seen from orbit, including parking lot counts, crop health, and night lights. Card Transaction Data explains how anonymized purchase records are aggregated and used to estimate consumer spending. Sensor and Shipping Data looks at physical readings from factories, trucks, and vessels, such as AIS pings and equipment telemetry. Mobile Location Data describes foot traffic and movement patterns derived from phone location signals, while Web Data Collection covers scraping and parsing of public pages, reviews, and job boards. A reader would start with the source most relevant to their question, then compare it against the others to see where signals overlap or conflict.
